clue.text: Smart little pullet! Not entirely

indicators.note: the word is not given in full, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a chick is a young bird, and a pullet is a young hen

explanation.surface: An admiring exclamation at a stylish young hen, then a grudging qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark makes the first two words read as one compliment; 'Smart' is in fact the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic describes something elegant and fashionable, which is the stylish sense of smart.

clue.text: Material from humorist was the opposite of entertaining for the audience

parts.note: a card is an amusing, witty person

indicators.note: what an audience hears, so the word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: to be entertaining is to amuse; the opposite is to have bored people

explanation.surface: A comedian's routine went down so badly that it sent the audience to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Bored and board sound the same, which is how a dull performance becomes a sheet of packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardboard is a stiff paper-based substance used for boxes, so it is a material.

clue.text: Could wildly silly person settle in this fantasy realm?

indicators.note: the word is jumbled as if thrown about wildly

parts.note: the letters of this word are the ones jumbled
a cuckoo is informally a crazy or foolish person
to land is to come to rest, as a bird settles

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question: might a fool make a home in some imaginary place?
explanation.walkthrough: The bird imagery of cuckoo and settling suits the phrase, which comes from Aristophanes' comedy The Birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloud-cuckoo-land is an idiom for an unrealistic dream world where impractical ideas flourish.

clue.text: Horse's hardtack

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., the famous American racehorse of the 1930s; the 's stands for 'is'
second meaning: hard dry biscuit carried as rations on ships

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive suggests food for a horse, but 'Horse's' is 'Horse is', and each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Ship's biscuit, or sea biscuit, is the sailors' name for hardtack; Seabiscuit was also a champion racehorse.

clue.text: Reptile exhausted circling eastern river

indicators.note: the word for exhausted goes round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: spent means tired out, used up

explanation.surface: A tired reptile swims around a river in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent is a snake, and snakes belong to the reptile class of animals.

clue.text: Positively declare tough youth turned away

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth in Edwardian-style dress, often seen as a tearaway

explanation.surface: Someone insists that a hard young man looked the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert the eyes or face is to turn them aside, so averted is a synonym.

clue.text: I persuade marketing boards to get better

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to board something is to get on it, so the word for persuade takes the marketing letters aboard

parts.note: to move someone can mean to sway or prompt them
PR, public relations, is the promotional side of business

explanation.surface: Someone claims to talk company directors round on matters of promotion so that results improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boards' looks like company boards but is a verb: one piece goes on board the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve is to become better in quality or condition.

clue.text: Encroaching tide flowing back

definitions.note: to back is a verb, as a wind backs when it turns round

indicators.note: letters set flowing are moved about into a new order

parts.note: these two words supply all fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The tide that was creeping up the beach starts to go out again.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sees the tide flowing back as one phrase; only 'back' is the definition, as when a wind backs.
explanation.definitionFit: When the wind backs it shifts anticlockwise, so to back is to alter course or turn round.

clue.text: Toss cycling pants

indicators.note: a letter goes round from the front of the word to the back

parts.note: to strew is to scatter or throw about

explanation.surface: An instruction to throw aside one's bike shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: Trews are close-fitting tartan trousers; 'pants' here means trousers in the American sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Trews are a Scottish form of trousers, and pants is the American word for trousers.

clue.text: Expedient note, one providing information

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a source is someone who supplies information, as to a journalist

explanation.surface: A handy memo from an informant.
explanation.definitionFit: An expedient is a means of dealing with a difficulty, as is a resource one can fall back on.

clue.text: 6 in European capital getting disease

indicators.note: the answer at 6 down: to change direction, here turning right into left

parts.note: Prague is the capital of the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: A traveller in a European capital falls ill.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference supplies the instruction: changing direction swaps R (right) for L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is an epidemic illness, most famously bubonic plague.

clue.text: Having diamonds in the place of gold primarily makes goof a lot of money

indicators.note: with the next phrase, says one letter is put where another was
the new letter takes the position the old one held

parts.note: to bungle is to make a mess of something

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used

parts.note: first letter only, the one to be replaced

explanation.surface: A jeweller's mistake of swapping gems for gold turns out very lucrative.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds. A bundle is informal for a large sum, as in 'made a bundle'.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a bundle is an informal idiom for earning a large sum of cash.

clue.text: However tense, start to spread ideas

parts.note: though can mean however, as in 'he came, though'

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: However tense things are, begin to share your concepts.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts are notions formed in the mind, which is what ideas are.

clue.text: Prominence of tipped-over rubbish

indicators.note: turned over, so the word is read backwards in this down clue

parts.note: rot means nonsense

explanation.surface: A heap of waste that has been knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prominence' sounds abstract but is a physical rise in the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky hill or outcrop, as on Dartmoor, so a prominence in the landscape.

clue.text: Settled exactly after article originally drafted by editor

indicators.note: the word for exactly comes after the article and its companion letter

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: only its first letter is taken
just means precisely

explanation.surface: An article first written up by an editor was finalised precisely.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adjusted has been fixed or regulated so it is in order, like a settled account.

clue.text: Last goal not oddly hurried

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are left out, keeping the even ones

parts.note: only its even-placed letters are kept

explanation.surface: A late winning strike was taken without any hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective describing the goal but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue or survive over time, the same as to endure.

clue.text: Issue leaders of newspapers covering yesterday's serious situation

parts.note: to issue is to come out, emerge

indicators.note: the front letters of each word, as leaders head a column

parts.note: the initial letters of these three words are taken

explanation.surface: Newspaper editorials reporting on yesterday's crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' suggests newspaper editorials, fitting the surface, but means initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency is a sudden dangerous crisis requiring immediate action.

clue.text: Old ship coated with preposterous blood colour is more sinister

indicators.note: the ship is covered by the colour, which goes round it
literally 'before-behind', back to front, so the word is reversed

parts.note: blood is red
Noah's ark, the ancient vessel

explanation.surface: An ancient vessel daubed in an absurd blood-red paint looks more menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: Preposterous comes from Latin for 'before-behind', a reversal signal beyond its usual meaning of absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Darker can mean more ominous or menacing, a figurative sense of less light.

clue.text: Well-chosen answer essentially recaptured

indicators.note: the essence, or heart, of the word: its central letters

parts.note: the two central letters of this ten-letter word are its heart

explanation.surface: A fitting response that was taken back.
explanation.definitionFit: An apt remark is suitable or appropriate to the occasion.

clue.text: Pistol raised on a Republican soldier

indicators.note: lifted up, so in a down clue the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a Luger is a German semi-automatic pistol
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Republican soldier with a gun held aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a professional soldier in a standing army, as opposed to a reservist.

clue.text: See about moving apart?

indicators.note: the letters are turned about into another order
the letters are moved around as well

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to be rearranged
taken as written, joining the other word's letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A question of whether to look into splitting up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: seeing about moving apart is what a couple who separate do.
explanation.definitionFit: To separate is to part company, as a couple who arrange to live apart.

clue.text: Area in Normandy above exposed part of cliff

parts.note: sur is French for on or above, and Normandy is in France
a cliff face is its bare vertical side

explanation.surface: A stretch of land on the Normandy coast overlooking a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface has extent, and in geometry area measures the size of a surface.

clue.text: Quarrel mounting over the Spanish packages

indicators.note: the quarrel word goes over the Spanish article, enclosing it
going up, so in a down clue the word reads upwards

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or squabble
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over Spanish packages.
explanation.definitionFit: Parcels are wrapped items sent by post, the same as packages.

clue.text: US force, through revised roster, becomes more efficient

indicators.note: the force letters go through the middle of the rearranged list
the list is redrawn, its letters rearranged

parts.note: the letters of this list are the ones rearranged
NG is the National Guard of the United States

explanation.surface: An American military unit improves its effectiveness thanks to a new duty rota.
explanation.definitionFit: Stronger means more powerful or capable, close to more effective.

clue.text: Wages of small company

definitions.note: plural noun; screw is British slang for a salary, treated as one sum

parts.note: a crew is a team or group of people

explanation.surface: The pay of a little firm.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw is old British slang for pay, as in 'a good screw'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a screw is a salary or wage, so it stands for someone's pay.

clue.text: Refreshing tip off for motor sport?

indicators.note: the tip, or first letter, is cut off

parts.note: bracing air is invigorating

explanation.surface: A cooling hint given at a motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip off' looks like a piece of inside information but is a deletion. The question mark marks motor sport as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing is a broader activity of which motor sport, such as Formula One, is one kind.

clue.text: Cancellation with reference to visit

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
to call on someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: A note calling off a planned visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A recall is a revocation or withdrawal, as of an order or a faulty product.

clue.text: Statesman, perhaps a Crimean, in trouble

indicators.note: the letters are in disarray, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words are the ones rearranged

explanation.surface: A political leader from Crimea is in difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Statesman' suggests a politician, but here it is a person from the States.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the United States, someone from the States, is an example of an American.

clue.text: Fierce eagles spotted principally in uncultivated region

parts.note: wild means savage or untamed
an erne is a sea eagle

indicators.note: the principal, or first, letter of the word is used

parts.note: only its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Savage eagles are sighted in the wilds.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilderness is wild land left unfarmed and unsettled.

clue.text: Inquisitive and loud without first hint of imagination

indicators.note: the following letter is left out

parts.note: noisy means making a lot of sound

indicators.note: the first letter of the word only

parts.note: only its first letter is the one dropped

explanation.surface: Someone prying and raucous, with no imagination at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosy person is too curious about other people's affairs.
